ai.title: Add PostHog analytics to CLI and backend
ai.summary: Integrates PostHog tracking into the CLI and backend services. Adds `posthog-node` dependency and initializes clients via new `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_API_KEY` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST_URL` environment variables. Tracks `cli.app_launched` on CLI start and `backend.prompt_sent` on WebSocket prompts, with user identification in the CLI. Ensures event flushing on graceful shutdowns and process exits in both surfaces.

eli5.text: The software now quietly tracks how people use it by sending anonymous usage data to a analytics service called PostHog. When you open the app, it logs that you started it, and when you send a message through the backend, it logs that interaction too. The data is only sent in production, and the system waits to make sure all the tracking information gets sent before it closes. If you are using the app, you probably won't notice anything different since this runs in the background.

ai.title: Add cli.login analytics event
ai.summary: Added `AnalyticsEvent.LOGIN` to track CLI authentication. The `Client` now calls `identifyUser` and `trackEvent` upon successful login, passing `fingerprintId`. This change affects `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts` and `npm-app/src/client.ts`.

eli5.text: When you log in to your Codebuff account from the command line, the system now quietly records that login event for analytics purposes. This means that each time you authenticate via the CLI, your user information is identified and a login event is tracked along with your device fingerprint. The change is already live today and applies to anyone using the CLI login flow. If you looked at the behavior, you would notice no visible difference in how login works - it simply happens in the background now.

ai.title: Update CLI startup and process logs
ai.summary: Startup messages in menu.ts now capitalize 'Codebuff' and guard cost mode output. dev-process-manager.ts changes 'development processes' to 'codebuff.json processes' and formats command failures with an em dash. background-process-manager.ts silences the gray log for killed processes.

eli5.text: When the assistant starts up and prints its opening messages, it now capitalizes the product name to 'Codebuff' and only shows the cost-mode notice when one is actually active, so the banner no longer spams a blank line. The startup log for the assistant's helper programs now calls them 'codebuff.json processes' instead of 'development processes', and when a helper fails to launch it prints the command name followed by an em dash and 'failed to start' instead of wrapping the command in backticks. While the assistant is shutting down, it stops printing the gray 'Killed process' line for each program it closes, so the terminal stays quieter during cleanup. These tweaks only change what you see in the terminal window while the assistant is starting, running, and stopping; no features or

ai.title: Hook up client logger
ai.summary: Added npm-app/src/utils/logger.ts wrapping pino to send analytics via trackEvent when eventId matches AnalyticsEvent. Backend logger updated to write to debug/backend.log and no longer exported. npm-app/src/client.ts now uses logger.info({ eventId: AnalyticsEvent.APP_LAUNCHED }) instead of trackEvent. New BACKGROUND_PROCESS_STARTED event added to common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts.

eli5.text: The app now keeps two kinds of logs in tidy, separate files instead of mixing them, so you can inspect detailed debug information for the backend (/debug/backend.log) and the app (/debug/npm-app.log) independently. Behind the scenes, a new analytics event called Background process started is now tracked, and the client uses a shared logger that automatically attaches your user id and session details to each log line. This means your logs are easier to read and the background work the app does can now be analyzed for reliability.

ai.title: Add analytics logging to background process manager
ai.summary: Analytics logging added to background process lifecycle in npm-app/src/background-process-manager.ts. Enum BACKGROUND_PROCESS_STARTED replaced with granular events START, END, CONTINUE, LEFTOVER_DETECTED in common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts. Logger context refactored from AsyncLocalStorage to global object in npm-app/src/utils/logger.ts, buffering events until user identification. flushAnalytics made async and awaited in CLI exit handlers.

eli5.text: The background process manager now sends more detailed analytics events to track lifecycle events like start, end, continue, and leftover detection. This gives better visibility into process behavior for debugging and monitoring. Users of the CLI tool will see these granular events logged instead of a single coarse 'background_process_started' event, improving diagnostic capabilities.

ai.title: Add clientRequestId to logger context
ai.summary: The `client.ts` module now assigns the generated `userInputId` to `loggerContext.clientRequestId`. This change links the unique client request identifier to the logging context, enabling trace correlation for debugging purposes. The update is scoped to `npm-app/src/client.ts`.

eli5.text: Every time you send a message to the assistant, the system now quietly tags that conversation with a unique tracking number. This number links your message to the behind-the-scenes logs so developers can trace what happened during your specific request if they need to debug an issue. If you were looking at the logs, you'd see this identifier attached to each session. It's a small, internal improvement that makes troubleshooting faster without changing how you interact with the assistant.

ai.title: Capitalize Codebuff in CLI strings and git author
ai.summary: String literals updated `codebuff` to `Codebuff` in CLI prompts, menu help, and git commit author. Affects `npm-app/src/checkpoints/file-manager.ts`, `npm-app/src/client.ts`, and `npm-app/src/menu.ts`. Mechanism: branding consistency. Git author name now matches product name.

eli5.text: Your copy of the assistant now refers to itself as "Codebuff" with a capital C everywhere you see it on screen and in git history. You'll notice the friendlier greeting messages and help text use the proper name, and any automatic code snapshots it saves will show "Codebuff" as the author instead of the lowercase version. This only tweaks how the product's name appears in its own menus and prompts - no features changed, just branding consistency.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.239
ai.summary: Version in `npm-app/package.json` bumped from 1.0.238 to 1.0.239. Internal release increment. No functional changes.

eli5.text: The assistant's software was given a new version number, like a car getting a new model year, even though nothing inside it actually changed how it works. This is a routine update that only affects the internal release process, so you would notice nothing different in how the assistant behaves or responds. It is live today as part of version 1.0.239, which also bundles a set of behind-the-scenes improvements like analytics tracking and logging that were added in recent days.

ai.title: codebuff 1.0.240
ai.summary: Bump codebuff version to 1.0.240. Updates `npm-app/package.json`. Internal release increment.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal version label was bumped to keep installs current with this release. Updating to this version gives you a smarter startup experience: you'll notice new analytics that help the team catch and fix problems faster, improved logging that makes errors easier to diagnose, and better tracking of your requests so issues can be traced and resolved more quickly.

ai.title: Fix imports in npm-app
ai.summary: Corrects import paths in `npm-app/src` to use relative paths or package aliases instead of `src/`. Updates `background-process-manager.ts`, `client.ts`, `analytics.ts`, and `logger.ts`. Fixes module resolution issues for the `common` package and internal `project-files` imports.

eli5.text: If you opened the app around 2025-04-25, you wouldn't notice anything different. This is behind-the-scenes housekeeping that fixes how parts of the app find and talk to each other, which helps keep things running smoothly for everyone using it.

ai.title: Add pino dependency to npm-app
ai.summary: Added `pino` version 9.4.0 to the dependencies in `npm-app/package.json`. This change prepares the package for structured logging implementation. Scope limited to the npm-app package configuration.

eli5.text: The assistant gained access to a new logging tool that will help it record events and activities in a more organized way, but it's only set up and not yet actively used in the app. This behind-the-scenes change affects the npm-app package and won't cause any visible behavior yet.

ai.title: Fix logger transport initialization in production
ai.summary: Refactored `npm-app/src/utils/logger.ts` to dynamically reinitialize `pinoLogger` when the production file transport is created or the project root changes. The logger instance is now mutable (`let`) and rebuilt with the correct transport (`productionFileTransport` vs `localFileTransport`) based on `NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT`. This ensures logs are written to the correct destination in production environments.

eli5.text: The production logging system was fixed so that activity logs now correctly route to the right destination in production environments. When the software runs in production and the project location changes, it rebuilds its log-writing settings with the correct transport; otherwise it continues using the local settings. If you looked now, production instances would record logs to the proper file instead of the local development path, while local and staging setups are unaffected.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.242
ai.summary: Version in `npm-app/package.json` bumped from 1.0.240 to 1.0.242. Reflects internal release progression. No functional changes, new features, or breaking modifications included.

eli5.text: An AI assistant tool quietly raised its internal version number from one release to the next, bundling a few small behind-the-scenes fixes that make the tool more reliable. This update corrects how parts of the tool talk to each other, adds improved logging for tracking errors, and includes an extra helper library for recording diagnostic information. There's nothing new you'd see directly, but installing this version keeps your copy current with the latest stability work.

ai.title: Disable logger on production
ai.summary: Logger initialization and analytics dispatch in `npm-app/src/utils/logger.ts` now unconditionally use `localFileTransport` during setup and return early if `NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT` is 'production'. This prevents production logging overhead and potential file transport errors by ensuring the logger remains disabled in prod environments. The change affects the `pinoLogger` instance and the `sendAnalyticsAndLog` function.

eli5.text: You won't see error messages or slowdowns from logging when you're using the production version, because the system now turns off its internal logging tool automatically in that environment. Behind the scenes, the logging feature checks if it's running in production and skips writing logs if so, reducing overhead and avoiding potential file errors. This is only active in production; in testing or development, logging continues as normally.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.243
ai.summary: Bumped npm-app/package.json version from 1.0.242 to 1.0.243. Internal release increment. Scope limited to npm-app package metadata.

eli5.text: The package label was bumped to 1.0.243, shipping today's fixes. With this update, analytics calls are suppressed when the assistant runs in production, so background usage tracking no longer fires while you're working. If you looked at the metadata file, you'd see only the version number change; the actual logging behavior change is what updating will give you.

ai.title: 1.0.244 disable local file logging in production
ai.summary: Version 1.0.244 conditionally disables pino local file transport when NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT is production. logger.ts initializes fileTransport as undefined in prod, skipping debug log writes to npm-app.log. sendAnalyticsAndLog removes early return guard, relying on transport state. Scope limited to npm-app package.

eli5.text: Starting with version 1.0.244, the app stops saving detailed debug logs to a local file when running in its live environment. If you are using the production version, logs that used to be written to a file called npm-app.log will no longer be saved there. Instead, the app only keeps logs in its active memory while it is running. This change affects anyone running the app in the production environment, which is now live today.

ai.title: Fix logger transport reinitialization for local environments
ai.summary: Refactored `npm-app/src/utils/logger.ts` to reuse `fileTransport` instead of creating a separate `productionFileTransport`. Logic now checks `!pinoLogger || !fileTransport` alongside project root changes to trigger reinitialization. This ensures the logger correctly handles transport state changes when switching between local and production contexts, preventing stale or missing transport instances.

eli5.text: The assistant's local logging tool no longer gets confused when switching between local development and production modes. Previously, it created a second separate log file handler for production that could go stale; now it correctly detects when the workspace changes and refreshes its log handler, so log entries from the appropriate context are captured without mixing or missing data. You won't see a visible change in the product itself, but the logging behavior is now more reliable behind the scenes.

ai.title: Pass userInputId to getDocumentationForQuery
ai.summary: Refactored `getDocumentationForQuery` to accept `userInputId` via options, removing internal `generateCompactId` calls. Updated `main-prompt.ts` to pass `promptId` as `userInputId` when invoking the function. This ensures consistent request tracking between documentation queries and main prompts.

eli5.text: Each time you ask the assistant a question, the system now tags the request with the exact same tracking number it uses for your main chat session, rather than inventing a new one on the spot. You won't see this yourself, but if someone checks the logs, they'll find documentation lookups tied cleanly to your session instead of scattered with separate IDs. The change is live today and affects every time the assistant pulls in documentation to answer your question.

ai.title: Refine agent instructions on endturn and code hygiene
ai.summary: Clarified `end_turn` usage in `backend/src/system-prompt/agent-instructions.md` to exclude system messages like tool results. Fixed formatting in 'Code Hygiene' section and removed obsolete 'User Questions' instruction.

eli5.text: The behind-the-scenes instructions that guide how the assistant decides when to stop responding were quietly tightened up. The assistant will now correctly stop talking after answering a question or when it's your turn to reply, but it won't mistakenly think it should stop just because a system message (like a tool result) arrived. The housekeeping rules for keeping code clean and readable were slightly reformatted, and an outdated instruction that told the assistant not to change anything when helping with ideas or questions was removed. Nothing changes for someone using the assistant today, but future responses should be slightly more reliable.

ai.title: Use raw stream on canceled response
ai.summary: Canceled responses now use raw chunk buffer instead of parsed buffer in npm-app/src/client.ts. Added rawChunkBuffer to store unprocessed stream chunks. On cancellation, assistant_message content uses rawChunkBuffer.join('').

eli5.text: When you cancel a response mid-stream, the system now uses the raw, unprocessed chunks of text instead of a cleaned-up version. This means the summary shown for the canceled response preserves the exact text as it arrived before any parsing happened. It's a small internal fix in the client code, and the only noticeable difference is that canceled responses reflect the original stream data rather than a reformatted copy.

ai.title: Fix CLI output formatting by collapsing excessive newlines
ai.summary: The CLI client now buffers response chunks and replaces sequences of three or more newlines with exactly two before writing to stdout. This change prevents visual clutter caused by excessive spacing in model outputs and tool call results. The backend utility `parse-tool-call-xml.ts` was also updated to join tool results with double newlines, aligning with the client-side normalization logic.

eli5.text: When you chat with the assistant in the terminal, the program now squeezes out any triple-or-bigger gaps of empty lines down to just two, so responses that used to sprawl with awkward blank space now read as tight, single-spaced blocks. The app collects each piece of the reply in a temporary note before printing, giving it a chance to tidy up the spacing first; tool results inside those replies get the same two-line treatment as they leave the assistant. Nothing about what information you receive changes, only how compactly it’s presented.

ai.title: Create log directory before writing logs
ai.summary: Logger now calls mkdirSync before initializing pino file transport. Prevents crashes when writing to debug or chat directories that do not yet exist. Affects npm-app/src/utils/logger.ts. Log path resolution moved to variable to support dynamic updates in production.

eli5.text: When you run the assistant, it now automatically creates the folders it needs to save log files before trying to write to them, instead of failing if those folders don't already exist. This matters for the logs saved to your computer's debug folder and for the chat logs saved in each project's own folder. You won't see this happen directly, but if you ever looked at when those log files first appeared, you'd no longer catch the assistant crashing because the folder wasn't there yet.

ai.title: Fix npm-app logger env check and mkdir path
ai.summary: Logger initialization in `npm-app/src/utils/logger.ts` and `backend/src/util/logger.ts` now checks `NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT === 'local'` instead of generic presence or production checks to enable file transports. `mkdirSync` call corrected to use `dirname(logPath)` instead of passing the transport object. Scope limited to backend and npm-app logger utilities.

eli5.text: The debugging log files that help developers track down problems in the local development tools now only turn on when the environment is explicitly set to a local development mode. Previously, the logs tried to write files in cases that didn't match the intended setup, causing errors when the log directory path was computed incorrectly. This fixes the local development experience so logs save properly when engineers are building and testing features, without affecting the live production environment.

ai.title: Remove unhandledRejection and uncaughtException listeners on CLI exit
ai.summary: CLI signal handlers now remove `unhandledRejection` and `uncaughtException` listeners before cleanup and exit. SIGHUP and SIGTERM handlers were unified into a loop to ensure this state reset occurs across all termination signals. This change prevents exceptions from being swallowed or re-triggered during the shutdown sequence in `npm-app/src/cli.ts`. The fix applies to the CLI package only.

eli5.text: When you close or stop the assistant's command-line tool, it now cleans up two kinds of error handlers that were left behind. Those handlers used to catch errors that occurred during shutdown, which could cause errors to be hidden or fired again while the tool was already trying to exit. This only affects the command-line tool and makes it shut down more reliably, though you probably wouldn't notice unless you were watching closely.

ai.title: Skip PostHog analytics in local
ai.summary: Added `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT !== 'local'` check in `npm-app/src/utils/logger.ts` to prevent PostHog analytics dispatch on local environments. Internal telemetry optimization to reduce noise and avoid accidental production data pollution during development.

eli5.text: When developers run the software on their own computers, the program now skips sending usage data to PostHog analytics. Previously, activity from local development environments, where developers are testing features, was being mixed into the same analytics stream as real user activity. This means you won't accidentally pollute production analytics with test data while coding locally.

ai.title: npm-app PostHog proxy routing and prod-only event filtering
ai.summary: npm-app PostHog client now routes events to `${NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL}/ingest` instead of `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST_URL`. trackEvent and identifyUser exit early unless `NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT` equals production. Scope covers npm-app analytics initialization and web redirect cleanup for /vibe.

eli5.text: Events you generate in the app, like which buttons you click or sign-ups, are now routed through our own server instead of going straight to PostHog. You won't notice anything change on your screen, but in the background your analytics now only ship when the app is running in the production environment; local or staging sessions quietly drop them. The proxy is already live, so production visits are already being filtered through the new path.

ai.title: Refactor pino logger setup in npm-app
ai.summary: Extracted pino logger initialization into setLogPath in npm-app/src/utils/logger.ts. Replaced manual transport and logger recreation with a helper that updates path and reinstantiates pino only on change. Removed getProjectRoot dependency; log path now derived directly from environment or current chat dir.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal logbook keeper was simplified so that it only rewrites the log file's location when that location actually changes, instead of recreating the whole logging setup every time it wrote a line. This is behind-the-scenes housekeeping in the developer tools, so you as a user won't see any visible difference in how the assistant behaves or where your logs are stored today.

ai.title: Fix affiliate referral link and code field
ai.summary: Affiliates page now uses snake_case `referral_code` from API response instead of camelCase `referralCode`. Link generation changed from `/referrals/${referralCode}?referrer=${userHandle}` to `/${userHandle}`. Removed error handling block for missing referral codes.

eli5.text: The affiliate referrals page now reads your referral code from the backend in a different format, and your personalized referral link is now just a simple link to your handle (for example, yourname.example.com) instead of a longer URL with a separate code in it. If you had previously seen an error message about a missing referral code, that message is gone. This is live today and affects the page that partners use to share their referral links.

ai.title: Add CODEBUFFGITHUBACTIONS env var to CI and logger
ai.summary: Introduced `CODEBUFF_GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` environment variable to CI workflows for `npm-app`, `backend`, and `common` test jobs. Updated `npm-app/src/utils/logger.ts` to skip `setLogPath` execution when this variable is set to true, preventing log file writes during CI runs. Scope limited to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `npm-app/src/utils/logger.ts`. This change ensures cleaner CI output by bypassing local log file persistence when running in GitHub Actions.

eli5.text: The system now stops writing log files to your computer when run inside automated testing tools. You wouldn't notice this directly, but if you looked at the testing setup, you'd see a special flag that tells the program to skip saving debug logs during tests. This keeps test output cleaner and prevents unnecessary file creation.

ai.title: localFileTransport skip in CI
ai.summary: localFileTransport disabled in GitHub Actions via CODEBUFF_GITHUB_ACTIONS env check. Prevents file logging overhead in CI environments. Affects backend/src/util/logger.ts.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs its internal checks in GitHub Actions, it will no longer write log files to disk, because that file-saving step is now turned off in that environment. If you triggered one of those automated runs today, you would see the same log output in the console but no log files created alongside it, which keeps those environments from filling up with extra data. This only affects those automated systems; everything else continues to save log files as before.

ai.title: Add origin to uncaught exception logs
ai.summary: The `uncaughtException` handler in `backend/src/index.ts` now accepts and logs the `origin` parameter. This provides context on where the exception occurred alongside the error, stack, message, and name in both console and structured logger output.

eli5.text: When something unexpected crashes your account's backend processes, you'll now see where that problem happened (like 'in the main app' or 'during a background task') along with the usual error details. This extra clue is written to both the on-screen logs you might watch and the structured records your system saves for later digging. The change only affects internal backend logs, so no visible buttons or features shift for anyone, but it does help anyone troubleshooting those rare crashes spot the cause faster.

ai.title: Create debug directory for local logging
ai.summary: Added mkdirSync call in backend/src/util/logger.ts to ensure debug directory exists before pino file transport initialization. Prevents logging errors in local environments when directory missing. Scope limited to backend logging utility.

eli5.text: When you run the software on your own computer for development work, it now silently creates a local folder to store debug logs so they don't cause errors. If you were watching the startup process, you might notice this folder appearing automatically where the logs are saved. This only affects people running the code locally during development, not the production software.

ai.title: Add structured logging to BigQuery init
ai.summary: Adds granular `logger.info` steps and structured `logger.error` payloads to `setupBigQuery` in `common/src/bigquery/client.ts` and `backend/src/index.ts`. Client instantiation moves from module load to `setupBigQuery`, with errors now re-thrown to trigger caller handling. Scope covers backend startup and shared BigQuery client logic.

eli5.text: When the backend service starts up, it now talks through each step of connecting to its data storage system instead of just quietly doing it. If something goes wrong during startup, you'll get a detailed error message with the specific failure code and what went wrong, rather than a vague 'failed to connect' message. This helps developers figure out why the service didn't start properly. The change is live today and affects anyone running or monitoring the backend service.

ai.title: Fix BigQuery client build errors
ai.summary: Added getClient() helper in common/src/bigquery/client.ts to enforce client initialization before use. Replaced direct client variable access with getClient() calls across insertTrace, insertRelabel, and query functions. Resolves build errors caused by potential undefined client access.

eli5.text: The analytics pipeline was intermittently crashing when trying to log new trace data before its database connection was fully ready. Now the system checks that the connection is established before allowing trace logging to proceed, which prevents those startup crashes. You would notice these crashes during brief moments when the system first starts up and attempts to record analytics before it's fully connected. If you saw sporadic logging failures in the background process, those are now resolved.

ai.title: Add error logging to analytics init, flush, track
ai.summary: Wraps initAnalytics, flushAnalytics, and trackEvent in try/catch blocks in backend/src/util/analytics.ts. Catches PostHog client errors, logs structured error data including stack, message, code, and details via logger.error, and re-throws only in initAnalytics. flushAnalytics and trackEvent swallow errors to prevent analytics failures from breaking application logic.

eli5.text: The app now quietly catches and records problems that happen when it sends usage data to the analytics system, instead of letting those hiccups crash the main features you rely on. If setup fails entirely, you'll still see an error stop things early, but everyday actions like tracking events or saving your progress won't break even if the analytics service is acting up. Behind the scenes, engineers get clearer error logs with details like what went wrong and where, so they can investigate without the whole app going down.

ai.title: Add troubleshooting guide for ENOTEMPTY install errors
ai.summary: Added 'Directory Not Empty' section to web/src/content/advanced/troubleshooting.mdx. Documents npm's `ENOTEMPTY` error during global installs, explaining it stems from leftover `.codebuff-*` temp directories in `node_modules`. Provides `rm -rf` command to clear the directory and retry installation. Also updated Discord community link to `https://codebuff.com/discord`.

eli5.text: If you ran into a stalling install error that mentioned a "Directory not empty" problem, the help pages now explain why it happens and how to clear the leftover temporary folder so the install can finish. When a package install gets interrupted, npm leaves behind a stray folder named something like.codebuff-XXXX in your global packages area; the updated guide shows you the exact command to delete that folder and then retry the installation. You would only notice this if you hit that specific error while installing, and the guidance is live for anyone who opens the troubleshooting page. The same update also refreshed the link to the community chat you can join if you need more help.

ai.title: Backend init sequence awaits BigQuery
ai.summary: Refactor `backend/src/index.ts` to wrap server startup in `async init()`. `setupBigQuery()` now awaits completion before `initAnalytics()` and `http.createServer()` run, preventing race conditions on startup. `analytics.ts` error logging formatted for consistency.

eli5.text: The server now waits for its data connection to finish setting up before it starts accepting requests, so the two parts can't step on each other during startup. If that data connection fails, the server logs the problem and keeps running instead of crashing. This is behind-the-scenes reliability work on the internal backend; outside developers won't see a new feature, just a more stable startup sequence.

ai.title: Generalize nodemodules troubleshooting paths
ai.summary: Updated `web/src/content/advanced/troubleshooting.mdx` to replace specific user paths (`/Users/my-user/...`) with generic placeholders (`/some/path/to/...`) in `npm ERR! ENOTEMPTY` examples. This change ensures documentation remains applicable to all users regardless of their local environment or node version manager setup. The fix affects only the Web docs surface.

eli5.text: The troubleshooting guide on the website previously showed example error messages using a specific person's computer file path (like /Users/my-user/...), which made the instructions confusing if you didn't use that exact setup. The guide now uses generic placeholders (like /some/path/to/...) so the steps make sense no matter what your computer or software version looks like. You won't notice this change while using the product itself, but if you ever run into this error and read the help guide online, the instructions will be clearer and more relevant to your situation.

ai.title: Log GOOGLEAPPLICATIONCREDENTIALS in backend env loader
ai.summary: Added a console.log statement in backend/src/env.mjs to print the value of process.env.GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS immediately after dotenv.config execution. This aids in debugging environment variable loading issues for Google Cloud credentials.

eli5.text: When the program starts up, it now prints a line showing where it expects to find Google's login key file. This only affects people who run the backend service themselves; if you just use the app normally, you won't see anything different.

ai.title: Add debug logging for GOOGLEAPPLICATIONCREDENTIALS
ai.summary: Added startup logging in `backend/src/env.mjs` to verify `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` resolution. Code reads the file path from env, logs contents on success, or reports missing file/variable on failure. This aids debugging credential loading issues.

eli5.text: When you start the assistant backend, it now checks whether your Google credentials file is set up correctly and prints out what it finds, either the file's contents or a clear message if the file or setting is missing. This only affects people running the backend locally or in a managed environment who rely on Google credentials for authentication. If you were ever seeing mysterious Google login errors, starting it up now shows the exact credential problem in the log instead of a vague failure. This is live today for anyone whose startup reads Google credentials.

ai.title: BigQuery client requires GOOGLEAPPLICATIONCREDENTIALS
ai.summary: setupBigQuery now throws if GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS is unset. Explicitly passes keyFilename to BigQuery constructor instead of relying on implicit ADC. Affects common/src/bigquery/client.ts.

eli5.text: The tool now checks that you've provided your Google login file before running, instead of silently trying to connect and failing later. If you run it without setting that file, it will stop early with a clear message naming the missing file. If you've set it, you'll now see a log line mentioning the file path as it connects. This applies to anyone running the BigQuery-backed parts of the tool; behavior is live today with no flags or rollout steps.

ai.title: BigQuery client passes parsed credentials instead of keyFilename
ai.summary: setupBigQuery now reads credentialsPath via fs.readFileSync and passes the parsed object to the BigQuery constructor alongside an explicit projectId, replacing the prior keyFilename option. The change requires GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID to be set, throwing if absent. Scope limited to common/src/bigquery/client.ts. Credentials are parsed at runtime rather than resolved by the client library from a file path.

eli5.text: The assistant now hands over your already-read cloud credentials directly when creating a BigQuery connection, instead of giving the library the file path and letting it read the file itself. If the required project identifier is missing from your environment, the setup stops early with a clear error instead of failing later in a confusing way.

ai.title: bigquery client log string concat
ai.summary: Replaced comma-separated logger.info arguments with string concatenation in common/src/bigquery/client.ts. Affects credential path and project ID logging. Internal formatting change only.

eli5.text: If you ever need to check the system's internal logs to see which cloud project your data is being sent to, the diagnostic messages about your project ID and credentials file path will now appear glued together on one line instead of on separate lines. This is purely a behind-the-scenes tweak to how those technical log lines are formatted when they're written, and it only affects what an engineer or advanced user would see if they were digging into the system's troubleshooting logs, no everyday feature or behavior changes for you.

ai.title: Add credential logging in BigQuery client setup
ai.summary: Added an info-level log statement in `common/src/bigquery/client.ts` to output parsed credentials during `setupBigQuery`. This change aims to assist in debugging credential loading issues. The modification is isolated to the core BigQuery client initialization logic.

eli5.text: The software now quietly prints out the contents of its password file as it starts up, so whoever is trying to fix a login problem can see exactly what credentials were picked up. You wouldn't see this yourself unless you were watching the behind-the-scenes log messages, but the text of the credentials will now appear in the system's log output each time it tries to connect to the database. This change is live today and only affects the diagnostic information that gets recorded, not the actual login process.

ai.title: Disable healthcheck and BigQuery setup
ai.summary: Healthcheck endpoint now returns 404. BigQuery setup function call commented out in initialization. Changes affect backend/src/index.ts. This disables health monitoring and data ingestion.

eli5.text: Starting today, the service status checker that was used for internal monitoring now returns a not-found response instead of saying everything is running fine, and the automatic connection to the analytics data warehouse has been turned off during startup. If you are an internal operator, any health monitoring tools you used to rely on will now report the service as unavailable, and data that was being automatically pulled from the database for reporting will no longer be ingested until it is manually re-enabled.

ai.title: Remove local-only guard from logger debug directory creation
ai.summary: The `env.NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT === 'local'` check is commented out in `backend/src/util/logger.ts`. The `mkdir` call for the debug directory now runs in all environments except GitHub Actions. This ensures debug directories are created even in production if the path is writable.

eli5.text: You probably won't notice anything different unless you use the software in a production environment where debug errors occur. Previously, the system only set up a special folder to save error details when running locally on a developer's machine; now it does so in more places - basically anywhere it's allowed to. This means if something goes wrong in production and the system can write to that folder, you're more likely to find detailed error logs to help figure out what happened.

ai.title: Backend init reverts to top-level, healthz 200, BigQuery uses ADC
ai.summary: Backend initialization moved from async `init()` to top-level execution. `/healthz` returns `ok` instead of `404`. `setupBigQuery` drops manual credential parsing, relying on Application Default Credentials. Logging setup restores `debug` dir creation for local environments and reverts verbose error wrapping in analytics.

eli5.text: The server is now easier to understand when something goes wrong: background setup tasks like database and analytics connections no longer crash the program if they fail, they just log an error and keep running, so your work is less likely to be disrupted. The health check endpoint, which tools use to confirm the server is alive, now correctly responds with 'ok' instead of appearing broken. Also, the program stopped printing your private Google login information in the logs, which is safer. If you run the server locally, developer debugging logs will be saved again to a 'debug' folder, making it easier for someone troubleshooting issues on your machine.

ai.title: Kill persistent PTY process on CLI exit
ai.summary: CLI exit handler now explicitly kills the persistent PTY process via `killAndResetPersistentProcess` before sending kill signals to background processes. This prevents orphaned PTY sessions and ensures cleaner shutdown. Exported `persistentProcess` from `terminal.ts` to allow direct access in `cli.ts`. Applies to `npm-app`.

eli5.text: When you close the assistant on this platform, it now makes sure to properly shut down the background terminal session it was using, instead of leaving it running and disconnected. Previously, this lingering session could cause cleanup issues or resource leaks; now it gets killed off cleanly during shutdown. You wouldn't notice anything different in normal use, but the system is more stable behind the scenes.

ai.title: Fix usage-based pricing, extract billing logic to @codebuff/billing
ai.summary: Pricing calculation fixed via new `@codebuff/billing` package, replacing scattered logic in `common/src/billing`. `message-cost-tracker.ts` defaults `centsPerCredit` to 1 if `userId` is null, preventing NaN errors for anonymous or unauthenticated requests. CI workflow updated to explicitly build `common` and `packages/billing` before typechecking. `backend` dependency added; old `auto-topup.ts` and direct `grant-credits` imports removed from backend middleware.

eli5.text: Anonymous users who interact with the assistant without signing in will no longer trigger pricing calculation errors, because the system now defaults to a flat 1 cent cost per credit when no user account is linked. The pricing logic has been moved out of the shared core code and into a dedicated billing module, which the backend now imports directly, and the continuous integration system has been updated to build this new module before running checks. The old standalone auto-top-up handling and direct credit-granting functions in the backend have been removed and replaced by the same shared module, keeping billing calculations consistent across the entire platform. This fix is live today.
